title: Pre AI SAT MBA
description: Stratified Pre-Assessment for MBA / PGDM Candidates (50 Questions)

sections.title: Section 1: AI Confidence & Perception
sections.description: Self-assessment of your AI usage and confidence (Unscored)

sections.title: Section 2: Applied AI Competencies
sections.description: Objective MCQs evaluating practical AI execution and judgment (40 Scored Questions)

questions.title: Self-Perception 1
questions.prompt: I can explain in plain terms what an AI model can and cannot reliably do (for example, why it may state wrong facts confidently).

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: Behavioural anchor per v7 4.2. Compared with LIT scored items to compute calibration.

questions.title: Self-Perception 2
questions.prompt: I can usually get a usable result in one or two prompts for tasks like summarising a report or drafting an email.

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: Task-level anchor, not an abstract 1 to 5. Paired with PROMPT scored items.

questions.title: Self-Perception 3
questions.prompt: I can use AI to find information and then check it against a reliable source before I rely on it.

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: Anchors verification behaviour, the core of this competency.

questions.title: Self-Perception 4
questions.prompt: I can use AI to rewrite the same message appropriately for very different audiences, such as a board and frontline staff.

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: Audience-adaptation anchor.

questions.title: Self-Perception 5
questions.prompt: I can direct AI to produce on-brand content in a specific structure I define.

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: Structure and brand anchor.

questions.title: Self-Perception 6
questions.prompt: I can set up a shared AI workspace so my team works from the same context instead of re-explaining it each time.

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: Persistent-context anchor.

questions.title: Self-Perception 7
questions.prompt: I can read a simple dashboard or AI analysis and judge whether its conclusion is actually supported by the numbers.

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: Non-tech decision-support anchor.

questions.title: Self-Perception 8
questions.prompt: I know what data is unsafe to put into public AI tools and when a human must approve an AI-driven action.

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: Governance and data-handling anchor.

questions.title: Self-Perception 9
questions.prompt: I can spot when an AI output is likely wrong and decide what to verify before acting on it.

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: The calibration-critical anchor; paired with the heaviest scored pool.

questions.title: Self-Perception 10
questions.prompt: I can set up an automation that reliably does the same thing every time it runs.

options.text: Not yet
Sometimes
Usually
Confidently and consistently

questions.rationale: Reliability anchor; the exact wording from the MBA addition Section 4.

questions.title: AI Literacy - Q1
questions.prompt: A manager asks an assistant for the market size of a niche B2B category and gets a confident figure attributed to a named report. Before it goes on a board slide, the safest assumption is:

options.text: The figure may be invented even with a named source, so verify it.
The figure is dependable because the assistant named a specific published report
Naming a source means the assistant retrieved the number from the live web
The confident, precise phrasing indicates the number came from real data

questions.rationale: A is correct because a named citation does not establish that the figure is accurate or that the model actually retrieved the cited report. AI can produce a plausible but invented figure or attribution. B and D rely on authority/confidence cues, while C assumes that naming a source proves live retrieval.

questions.title: AI Literacy - Q2
questions.prompt: Which statement about large language models is FALSE?

options.text: They generate likely next text rather than retrieving verified facts from a database
After training, a model continuously updates itself as new events occur worldwide
They can write fluent, well-structured prose that is nonetheless factually wrong
A larger context window lets the model consider more input material at once

questions.rationale: Spot-the-false with three true statements removes the coin-flip of a plain T/F.

questions.title: AI Literacy - Q3
questions.prompt: Which pairing of AI capability and primary category is INCORRECT?

options.text: A source-grounded research system is used for document-based evidence retrieval
A workflow orchestration platform is used to connect applications and run multi-step processes
A presentation-generation system is primarily an automation platform
An AI app-prototyping environment is used to build AI-powered applications

questions.rationale: Reframed to test capability-to-category understanding without relying on product-name recognition.

questions.title: AI Literacy - Q4
questions.prompt: The amount of text a model can consider at one time, input and output together, is its ____.

options.text: training cutoff date
system prompt length
output temperature setting
context window size

questions.rationale: Deliberately easy anchor item; all four options are real terms of similar length.

questions.title: Prompt Engineering - Q5
questions.prompt: You want a structured, source-honest competitor summary. Which prompt is strongest?

options.text: Act as a senior analyst and write a thorough, insightful competitor landscape review
For the three competitors, return a table of positioning, pricing and weakness
Produce a comprehensive, professional competitor analysis covering every relevant angle
Analyse our competitors in depth and tell me everything important I should know

questions.rationale: The correct option is not the longest; the others are padded with adjectives that add no constraint.

questions.title: Prompt Engineering - Q6
questions.prompt: To classify incoming support messages into three fixed categories consistently, the most reliable technique is:

options.text: Increase the temperature so the model varies how it reads each message
Instruct the model to be accurate and consistent in every classification
Supply a few labelled examples showing each category in use
Write a longer role description casting it as a support specialist

questions.rationale: Tests few-shot against three plausible-sounding but non-functional levers.

questions.title: Prompt Engineering - Q7
questions.prompt: For a multi-step business decision, which approach makes the analysis easiest for a reviewer to check?

options.text: Ask for a final recommendation only, so the answer stays concise
Ask for assumptions, calculations, evidence, criteria, and a separate recommendation
Ask the model to sound highly confident so the decision is easier to communicate
Ask the model to produce a longer answer regardless of how the analysis is structured

questions.rationale: Tests structured reasoning and verification rather than asking for visible chain-of-thought. The correct approach makes the load-bearing assumptions, evidence and decision basis inspectable.

questions.title: Prompt Engineering - Q8
questions.prompt: A prompt reads: write a launch post that is professional but fun, short but detailed, formal but casual. The core defect is:

options.text: It sets contradictory constraints that cannot all be met
It never assigns the model a role or a target audience for the post
It is too brief to give the model enough material to work with
It supplies no worked example of the tone the team actually wants

questions.rationale: A, C and D are all real prompt weaknesses, so the learner must pick the fatal one.

questions.title: AI Research & Info Retrieval - Q9
questions.prompt: You need a defensible market-size figure for an investor pitch. The soundest approach is:

options.text: Quote the model's figure directly, noting the confidence level it expressed
Trace the estimate to a primary source and confirm it
Average the figures returned by three different assistants for balance
Use the first search result that appears for the same market question

questions.rationale: C looks methodical but averages unverified guesses.

questions.title: AI Research & Info Retrieval - Q10
questions.prompt: You have 15 uploaded reports and need answers cited back to passages in those exact files. Best fit:

options.text: An open-web research assistant that searches and cites external pages
A presentation system that turns written material into formatted slides
A source-grounded research assistant that cites the uploaded corpus
A shared documentation workspace that drafts and searches team material

questions.rationale: Tests exact-corpus retrieval and citation needs without depending on recognition of a particular product name.

questions.title: AI Research & Info Retrieval - Q11
questions.prompt: For a current-events question needing live web pages with links, the better fit is:

options.text: A plain assistant with no browsing tool, relying on its trained knowledge
A slide-design tool that formats findings into a presentation layout
A workflow tool that moves data between the applications you already use
A search-grounded assistant that browses and cites live pages

questions.rationale: Distinguishes trained knowledge from live retrieval.

questions.title: AI Research & Info Retrieval - Q12
questions.prompt: A manager prompts for five statistics proving our market is growing and pastes them into a deck. The main methodological flaw is:

options.text: The prompt asks only for confirming evidence, inviting cherry-picking
Five statistics is too small a set to support a market-level claim
The request should have specified a date range for the statistics used
A general assistant was used rather than a dedicated research tool

questions.rationale: All four read as reasonable critiques; only B names the confirmation-seeking flaw.

questions.title: AI Communication - Q13
questions.prompt: You must brief a non-technical board on an AI pilot. The best use of AI is to:

options.text: Forward the raw technical report so the board sees the full evidence base
Read the full report aloud in the meeting so nothing is left out
Produce a plain-language summary with a recommendation, then verify it
Present only the charts and let the board draw its own conclusions

questions.rationale: Tests audience adaptation together with the verification step.

questions.title: AI Communication - Q14
questions.prompt: You need a polished pitch deck quickly from a rough outline. Best fit:

options.text: A source-grounded document-research system
A workflow-orchestration platform
A speech-generation system that converts written scripts to audio
An AI presentation system for editable decks from outlines

questions.rationale: Each distractor names a real capability category, so the item tests capability-to-task fit rather than product recognition.

questions.title: AI Communication - Q15
questions.prompt: You want a presenter-style explainer video without filming anyone. Best fit:

options.text: An AI avatar-video system that turns a script into presenter video
A search-grounded research system that answers with cited live sources
An AI data-analysis system that analyses spreadsheet data
A shared documentation workspace that drafts and organises documents

questions.rationale: Tests capability-to-task fit across distinct tool categories without product-name recognition.

questions.title: AI Communication - Q16
questions.prompt: A team sends an AI-drafted client email unedited and it opens with as an AI language model. The right lesson is:

options.text: The team should stop using AI for any client-facing correspondence
AI drafts need human review; a person sends the final version
The team should switch to a different model and send the draft again
The prompt needed more detail about the client and the desired tone

questions.rationale: D is a strong near-miss that fixes the draft but not the missing review step.

questions.title: AI Content Creation - Q17
questions.prompt: A social-post agent should return caption and image prompt as separate fields but returns them merged in one block. The defect is:

options.text: The caption is shorter than the campaign brief actually calls for
The hashtags chosen do not match the audience the post is aimed at
Caption and image prompt are merged, blocking the next step
The caption tone is inconsistent with the brand voice guide in use

questions.rationale: Grounded in the structured-output pattern; distractors are real content critiques.

questions.title: AI Content Creation - Q18
questions.prompt: The most reliable way to keep AI content on-brand across a team is to:

options.text: Ask the model politely for on-brand writing at the start of each task
Move to a larger model that has seen more marketing copy in training
Raise the temperature so the writing gains more personality and flair
Give it a saved brand-voice guide and a few approved examples

questions.rationale: C is the plausible model-size fallacy.

questions.title: AI Content Creation - Q19
questions.prompt: You want a shareable interactive one-pager generated from a chat and editable through further prompts. Best fit:

options.text: A conversational AI environment for creating and editing artifacts
A speech-generation system that turns written scripts into spoken audio
A workflow-orchestration platform that links applications together
A search-grounded research system that answers from live web sources

questions.rationale: Tests the interactive-artifact capability rather than recognition of the product name.

questions.title: AI Productivity & Knowledge Mgmt - Q20
questions.prompt: Your team re-pastes the same company background into every new chat. The better setup is to:

options.text: Train everyone to paste the background faster at the start of each chat
Hold the shared context in a persistent Project used for new chats
Write one very long prompt that carries all the background each time
Circulate the background by email before each working session begins

questions.rationale: Persistent context versus three plausible workarounds.

questions.title: AI Productivity & Knowledge Mgmt - Q21
questions.prompt: You want a central place for the team’s living documents with AI help to write and search them. Best fit:

options.text: A presenter-video generation system
A speech-generation system
A shared AI workspace for drafting, editing, and search
A workflow-orchestration platform that connects applications

questions.rationale: Tests the intended shared-document and knowledge-work capability without product-name recognition.

questions.title: AI Productivity & Knowledge Mgmt - Q22
questions.prompt: Two teammates get different AI answers about the same policy. The most likely cause and fix is:

options.text: One is on a paid plan with a stronger model, so upgrade the other user
They used different assistants, so standardise the team on a single brand
Outputs vary run to run, so simply retry until the two answers match
They used different context, so keep the policy in one shared source

questions.rationale: D is a real phenomenon misapplied as the cause, which makes it tempting.

questions.title: Data Analysis & Decision Support - Q23
questions.prompt: A dashboard shows revenue up 20% while gross margin fell 10 points. The most accurate read for the CEO is:

options.text: The business is clearly healthier, since the top line has grown strongly
Margin matters less than revenue, so the trend should be read positively
Sales grew but each sale earns less, so examine discounting and cost
The margin figure is likely a reporting error and should be recalculated

questions.rationale: Requires holding two metrics together rather than reading the flattering one.

questions.title: Data Analysis & Decision Support - Q24
questions.prompt: It costs 5,000 to acquire a customer who returns 4,000 in lifetime value. The unit economics are:

options.text: Healthy, since each customer still contributes meaningful revenue overall
Acceptable provided the company acquires a large enough customer base
Impossible to judge without knowing the company's total annual revenue
Unsustainable: acquisition cost is higher than lifetime value

questions.rationale: Difficulty: Medium-hard. Bloom Apply. C is the scale fallacy; D states the correct unit-economics conclusion.

questions.title: Data Analysis & Decision Support - Q25
questions.prompt: A bar chart's vertical axis starts at 90, making a 2% rise look dramatic. The issue is:

options.text: The axis starts at ninety, so a two percent rise appears far larger
The colour scheme makes the smaller bars difficult to read accurately
Too few bars are shown to establish whether a real trend exists at all
The chart has no legend explaining what each of the bars represents

questions.rationale: Distractors are all genuine chart criticisms.

questions.title: Data Analysis & Decision Support - Q26
questions.prompt: AI notes that ice-cream sales and customer churn both rose in summer and suggests ice cream causes churn. The correct judgment is:

options.text: Act on the insight, since the model identified a real repeating pattern
Correlation is not causation; a seasonal driver may explain both
Buy external ice-cream market data to test the relationship properly
Trust it, since the model examined more data than a person could review

questions.rationale: C is the seductive do-more-research answer that accepts the false premise.

questions.title: Responsible AI - Q27
questions.prompt: You want to summarise an NDA-covered client contract using a public consumer AI tool. The right action is:

options.text: Paste it in, since summarising a contract is a low-risk routine task
Paste only selected clauses so the whole contract is never exposed at once
Paste it and instruct the assistant not to retain or reuse the content
Keep NDA material out of unapproved tools; use approved systems or redact

questions.rationale: C and D are sophisticated half-measures that still breach the obligation.

questions.title: Responsible AI - Q28
questions.prompt: Which action most needs a human approval step before an AI workflow executes it?

options.text: Issuing a refund or making a financial or legal commitment
Automatically tagging and filing incoming email by topic and sender
Drafting a suggested reply that a person will read before it is sent
Producing a written summary of a meeting for the team's own records

questions.rationale: Separates irreversible committing actions from reversible internal ones.

questions.title: Responsible AI - Q29
questions.prompt: A client asks whether AI was used in preparing the report, and the engagement requires transparency about material AI assistance. Choose the BEST and the WORST response.

options.text: Say the work was produced entirely by the team without any AI help
Decline to discuss the tools and methods used to prepare the report
Confirm that AI assisted and that a human reviewed and stands behind the work
Confirm AI was used and attribute any errors in it to the AI system

questions.rationale: C is transparent while retaining human responsibility. A is the worst because it makes a false statement; D also avoids responsibility, while B withholds relevant information.

questions.title: AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement - Q30
questions.prompt: AI gives a five-step market-entry recommendation for the board. The soundest first verification step is:

options.text: Check the document for grammar, structure and formatting consistency
Identify the load-bearing assumption or number and verify it
Convert the recommendation into slides so the board can review it quickly
Ask the assistant to confirm whether it is confident in its own recommendation

questions.rationale: D is the fake check that feels like diligence.

questions.title: AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement - Q31
questions.prompt: AI states: revenue grew from 2 crore to 3 crore, a 50% rise, so we are on track to double next year. The flawed step is:

options.text: The fifty percent figure has been calculated incorrectly from the two numbers
The figures should be stated in a single consistent currency and unit
Assuming one period's growth rate repeats into a doubling is unjustified
Growth should be compared against the sector rather than the prior year

questions.rationale: The arithmetic is sound; D is a reasonable-sounding but different critique.

questions.title: AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement - Q32
questions.prompt: For a risky decision you get two answers: one hedges and names what to verify, one is crisp and absolute. By default the more trustworthy is:

options.text: The absolute answer, since a clear recommendation is easier to act upon
Whichever is longer, since it covers more of the relevant ground
Whichever came first, since later answers tend to drift off topic
The hedged answer, because it signals uncertainty and names checks

questions.rationale: Counters the bias that confidence signals correctness.

questions.title: AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement - Q33
questions.prompt: The single most important habit before acting on a high-stakes AI output is to:

options.text: Independently verify the facts or the logic the output rests on
Reformat the output so it reads cleanly for the intended audience
Ask a second AI tool to rewrite the same output for comparison
Save a copy of the output so the reasoning can be reviewed later

questions.rationale: Deliberate easier anchor in a hard-leaning pool.

questions.title: AI Workflow Automation - Q34
questions.prompt: Put the basic support-bot flow into the correct order.

options.text: Agent decides, message arrives, reply delivered, then the send tool runs afterwards
Message arrives, agent decides, send action runs, reply is delivered
Send tool runs, message arrives, reply delivered, then the agent decides content
Message arrives, reply delivered, agent decides, then the send tool runs at the end

questions.rationale: Four complete orderings of equal length, so sequence rather than fragments is tested.

questions.title: AI Workflow Automation - Q35
questions.prompt: A support bot writes its reply into the run log but customers receive nothing. The likely cause is:

options.text: The model chosen is too small to generate a reply of sufficient quality
The trigger fired twice, so the two replies cancelled each other out
The agent produced text but never called the send action
The memory buffer grew too large and dropped the outgoing message

questions.rationale: Generating text is not the same as taking the action, the central chatbot lesson.

questions.title: AI Workflow Automation - Q36
questions.prompt: Which task is the best first candidate to automate?

options.text: A rare, judgment-heavy negotiation where the stakes differ every time
A one-off creative brainstorm the team runs once for each campaign
A sensitive termination decision requiring careful individual handling
A frequent, rule-based step such as routing incoming form submissions

questions.rationale: Tests fit-for-automation judgment rather than automate-everything enthusiasm.

questions.title: AI APIs & Integrations - Q37
questions.prompt: In plain terms, an API lets:

options.text: A model access more training data so that its answers steadily improve
Two software tools exchange data or trigger actions in one another
A model's text output be converted into a format a person can read
A workflow store the results it produces so they can be retrieved later

questions.rationale: A is the common misconception that integration improves the model itself.

questions.title: AI APIs & Integrations - Q38
questions.prompt: Your workflow needs to generate an image from an external service mid-run. This is done by:

options.text: Copying the output by hand from the image service into the workflow each run
Emailing the request to the image service and waiting for the file to return
Call the external service's API from the workflow
Capturing the image from the service screen and attaching it to the record

questions.rationale: Grounded in the image-service call pattern from the build.

questions.title: Agentic AI - Q39
questions.prompt: What distinguishes an AI agent from a plain chatbot?

options.text: It runs on a larger model trained on more varied material than a chatbot
It can take actions and use tools to complete a task, not only reply
It responds more quickly because it processes requests in parallel
It retains memory of the user across separate, unrelated conversations

questions.rationale: D is a strong trap: memory is not the same as agency.

questions.title: Agentic AI - Q40
questions.prompt: A single agent handles the whole support flow well. Adding a second coordinating agent is justified:

options.text: Whenever possible, since additional agents increase overall system capability
When the existing agent runs too slowly to meet demand at peak times
When the work splits into distinct sub-tasks that benefit from hand-off
When the system needs to appear more sophisticated to external reviewers

questions.rationale: C is a real-sounding performance rationale that agents do not solve.
